description: Rubric for evaluating how well the tau-voice user simulator approximates a real human caller. Rate each dimension on a 1-4 scale.
instructions: Listen to the full conversation audio. The CALLER is synthetic; the AGENT is an AI customer service rep. Rate how well the CALLER approximates natural human behavior on each dimension (1-4). Focus on the caller, not the agent.

calibration.description: A score of 4 = a real human caller. A score of 1-2 = a clearly robotic system like the example below.

anchor_high.label: A real human caller on a customer service phone call.

dimensions.name: Voice & Prosody Quality
dimensions.short_description: Does the voice sound natural in quality, intonation, pacing, and expressiveness?
dimensions.description: Rate the caller's voice (timbre, articulation) and delivery (intonation, rhythm, emphasis, emotion). Natural speakers adjust prosody to context — questions rise, frustration sharpens pace, account numbers are slow and deliberate.

1.label: Poor
1.description: Noticeably synthetic — robotic quality, unnatural pronunciation, or artifacts. Flat or inappropriate delivery with little variation in pitch, pace, or emphasis.

2.label: Below Average
2.description: Some natural qualities but synthetic traits dominate. Prosody feels mechanical — a 'reading aloud' cadence, forced emotion, or misplaced emphasis. More artificial than natural.

3.label: Above Average
3.description: Good approximation for most of the conversation. Generally adjusts pace, tone, and emphasis to context. Some noticeable drops — unnaturally even pacing, a flat emotional response, or an off-sounding word — but outweighed by convincing sections.

4.label: Excellent
4.description: Closely approximates natural speech throughout. Realistic texture, natural articulation, rich prosody — speeds up when excited, slows when thinking, modulates tone with emotion. No significant shortcomings.

dimensions.name: Audio Environment Realism
dimensions.short_description: Does the audio environment sound like a real phone call?
dimensions.description: Rate the realism of background noise, phone line quality, and incidental sounds (coughs, nearby speech). Real phone calls have imperfect audio — some noise, slight telephony distortion, occasional environmental interruptions.

1.label: Poor
1.description: Obviously fake. Background noise loops, appears/disappears abruptly, or is implausible. Incidental sounds feel synthetic or poorly timed. Does not resemble a real call.

2.label: Below Average
2.description: Some realistic elements but unconvincing overall. Noise feels layered on rather than natural — poor blending, too-consistent volume, or filter-like phone quality. More artificial than natural.

3.label: Above Average
3.description: Convincing for most of the call with some imperfections — looping noise, a slightly out-of-place sound, or inconsistent telephony quality. Noticeable but the environment still leans believable.

4.label: Excellent
4.description: Closely approximates a real phone call. Noise varies naturally, phone quality feels authentic, incidental sounds are well-integrated. No significant shortcomings.

dimensions.name: Turn-Taking Naturalness
dimensions.short_description: Is the timing of when the caller starts and stops speaking natural?
dimensions.description: Rate the rhythm of the conversation — response delays, pause lengths, overall pacing. Real callers vary their timing: quick replies to simple questions, longer pauses after complex information.

1.label: Robotic
1.description: Mechanical timing — same delay regardless of context, or unnatural silences followed by sudden speech. Feels like two recordings played in sequence.

2.label: Awkward
2.description: Timing is off for most of the conversation — too fast, too slow, or unnaturally uniform. Variation exists but doesn't match context. More rigid than natural.

3.label: Somewhat Natural
3.description: Natural for most exchanges with some variation. A few off moments — an oddly long pause, a too-consistent delay, or a too-quick response after complex info. Overall rhythm leans natural.

4.label: Natural
4.description: Natural throughout — quick acknowledgments, thoughtful pauses, appropriate hesitation. The rhythm has the organic ebb and flow of a real call. No significant shortcomings.

dimensions.name: Backchannel Naturalness
dimensions.short_description: Are listener signals (mm-hmm, uh-huh, okay) natural and well-timed?
dimensions.description: Rate the caller's backchannel signals — 'mm-hmm', 'uh-huh', 'okay', 'got it'. These matter most during longer agent speech (explanations, reading details). They are NOT expected during short responses or quick exchanges — real people don't backchannel every turn.

1.label: Absent or Disruptive
1.description: Never backchannels (even during long agent speech) OR backchannels at wrong moments — mid-word, over important info, or in random positions.

2.label: Poorly Timed
2.description: Backchannels exist but mostly poorly placed — mid-sentence, mechanically regular, or forced. May backchannel unnecessarily during short responses or stay silent during long explanations. More awkward than natural.

3.label: Somewhat Natural
3.description: Reasonably placed for most of the conversation. Some issues — a mistimed backchannel, a too-long silence during a lengthy explanation, or a slightly too-regular pattern. Limited variety of tokens. Leans convincing overall.

4.label: Natural
4.description: Closely approximates natural listening. Appears during longer speech at right moments, absent during short exchanges. Frequency adapts to the conversation. No significant shortcomings.

dimensions.name: Interruption Behavior
dimensions.short_description: Are the caller's interruptions natural and well-motivated?
dimensions.description: Rate whether interruptions are well-timed and motivated. Valid reasons: agent is rambling, repeating known info, going off track, or the caller has heard enough to respond. Interrupting while the agent conveys new, important info is inappropriate. Note: when both speak at once, the user may continue — yielding is the agent's job. If no interruptions occur, rate whether that absence feels natural.

1.label: Disruptive
1.description: Interruptions are clearly inappropriate — cuts off the agent for no reason, interrupts during important info, or never interrupts even when the agent rambles excessively. Feels mechanical.

2.label: Awkward
2.description: Noticeably unnatural — interrupts too early or at bad moments, or is too passive when the agent repeats itself. More mechanical than natural.

3.label: Somewhat Natural
3.description: Most interruptions feel motivated and reasonably timed. Some noticeable moments — an unmotivated interruption or one that comes slightly too early. Majority of behavior is convincing.

4.label: Natural
4.description: Interruptions are well-motivated and timed at natural points. Interrupts when appropriate, holds back when the agent is conveying useful info. No significant shortcomings.

dimensions.name: Behavioral Plausibility
dimensions.short_description: Does the caller behave like a real person would?
dimensions.description: Rate whether the caller is believable as a real customer. Consider patience levels, emotional reactions to delays or mistakes, and genuine engagement vs. scripted behavior.

1.label: Scripted
1.description: Behaves like a machine — infinitely patient, no emotional reactions, information delivered in a robotic sequence. No genuine engagement.

2.label: Stilted
2.description: Predominantly unrealistic — too patient with errors, no frustration when warranted, flat affect. Occasional human moments but overall feels overly cooperative and tolerant.

3.label: Somewhat Plausible
3.description: Behaves like a real person most of the time. Some off moments — too patient after a long delay, too-consistent engagement, or missing pushback where expected. Leans convincingly human.

4.label: Convincing
4.description: Believable throughout — patience has limits, shows genuine relief or frustration, engagement waxes and wanes. Pushes back when appropriate. No significant shortcomings.

dimensions.name: Speech Accuracy
dimensions.short_description: Was the text actually said? Does the spoken audio match the caller's transcript?
dimensions.description: Rate how faithfully the synthesized audio renders the caller's intended text (the transcript). This is a SYNTHESIS-fidelity check, not a judgment of word choice — read the transcript and compare it to what you hear. Look for dropped, mangled, duplicated, or skipped words; mispronounced or garbled numbers, order IDs, emails, and names; truncated or cut-off utterances; or words rendered in the wrong language.

1.label: Inaccurate
1.description: Frequently fails to say the text — significant words dropped or garbled, key details (numbers, IDs, names) mispronounced or unintelligible, or utterances truncated. Hard to follow what the caller meant to say from the audio alone.

2.label: Several Errors
2.description: Several noticeable mismatches between transcript and audio — multiple mangled words or a mispronounced critical detail (an order ID, email, or number) that could mislead the agent. More error-prone than clean.

3.label: Mostly Accurate
3.description: Audio matches the text for most of the call with minor slips — an occasional swallowed word, a slightly off pronunciation, or one shaky detail — but nothing that obscures meaning or misleads the agent.

4.label: Accurate
4.description: The audio faithfully says the text throughout. All words present, numbers/IDs/names pronounced clearly and correctly, no truncation. No significant shortcomings.

dimensions.name: Phrasing Naturalness
dimensions.short_description: Is the wording itself what a real person would say (independent of how it sounds)?
dimensions.description: Rate the caller's WORD CHOICE and sentence construction as TEXT — judge the transcript, not the audio. This isolates phrasing problems (what the simulator wrote) from synthesis problems (how it was spoken, covered by Voice & Prosody). A line can be voiced perfectly yet still be phrased like no real caller would speak. Look for stilted or over-formal wording, robotic or templated constructions, assistant-style LLM-isms ('I'd be happy to', 'Certainly!', 'As an AI'), over-complete or over-explained sentences, and repetitive phrasing.

1.label: Robotic
1.description: Wording reads like a script or a chatbot — over-formal, templated, or full of assistant-style phrasing. No real caller would talk this way.

2.label: Stilted
2.description: Phrasing is unnatural for most of the call — overly complete sentences, formal word choice, or repeated canned constructions. Occasional natural lines but stilted phrasing dominates.

3.label: Mostly Natural
3.description: Wording sounds like a real caller most of the time. Some off moments — an over-formal sentence, a slightly templated turn, or a mild LLM-ism — but the majority is convincingly conversational.

4.label: Natural
4.description: Word choice and sentence construction read like a real person throughout — conversational, appropriately terse, contractions and casual phrasing where expected. No significant shortcomings.

metadata_fields.description: Unique identifier for the conversation being evaluated
Unique identifier for the human evaluator
The domain of the conversation (airline, retail, telecom)
The voice persona used for the simulated caller
The voice agent provider being used in the conversation
Whether the conversation contains any speech overlap or interruption events

optional_fields.description: Any additional observations — specific moments that were particularly convincing or unconvincing.
